expectations.text: Argues reach and relationship value in place of a registration claim
expectations.evidence: The response swaps the registration claim for reach and relationship value: 'reach asset', a list of four values that 'none depends on ticket conversion' (reach beyond the room, archive, speaker value, sponsor/partner inventory), and a decision request to approve investment 'on its reach and archive value'. It argues this replacement directly. It does not reach a full 5 because two of the relationship points are hedged: speaker value is labelled 'a hypothesis… not a claim' and sponsor inventory is left in brackets. The 'relationship' part of the argument is therefore thin and partly unasserted

expectations.text: Argues reach and relationship value in place of a registration claim
expectations.evidence: The page swaps the sales claim for a reach claim. It says: 'We are therefore calling the channel a reach and ticket-page exposure channel. We will not call it "top of funnel for ticket sales" until the data supports that wording.' It also asks the board to 'Approve the channel as a reach investment on the current evidence.' The reach case is backed by an owned audience of 12k subscribers and 40% year-over-year view growth. Relationship value is barely argued. The closest line is 'Subscribers are an owned audience... new talks reach them at no extra cost.' Nothing covers community, trust, or on
